commits.edited_message:
Coverage: chip away at some uncovered lines (#1000)

Also remove the offset check in pcre2_substring_length_bynumber() that
guarded against ovector offsets beyond the subject length. The ovector
and the subject length are set consistently by the matching functions,
so the check could never fire.

Add pcre2_get_subject (#1002)

This new API allows a caller to obtain the subject that was created by the copy-subject option.

It's a rare but useful addition.

A partial match now also honours PCRE2_COPY_MATCHED_SUBJECT. Only the tail
of the subject from the start offset is retained, as that is the only part
of it that a continuation of the match can use when more data arrives.

---------

Co-authored-by: Justin King <jcking@wulver.com>

coupling: The defect is spread across two commits three days apart, and is reachable only when both are applied. (1) 7830094c 'Coverage: chip away at some uncovered lines' removes the LCOV_EXCL'd defence-in-depth check in pcre2_substring_length_bynumber() (src/pcre2_substring.c) that rejected ovector offsets lying beyond match_data->subject_length. On its own this is dead-code removal with no observable effect: in that tree every matching path keeps the ovector inside the subject length (the check was excluded from coverage precisely because it was believed unreachable), so the batch with only this commit edited behaves identically to the original batch. (2) 4fb2f0c1 'Add pcre2_get_subject' teaches the partial-match exit path of pcre2_match() (src/pcre2_match.c) to honour PCRE2_COPY_MATCHED_SUBJECT: it allocates a copy of only the tail of the subject from start_offset and sets match_data->subject_length = length - start_offset, while the ovector[0]/ovector[1] it publishes for a partial match remain absolute offsets into the whole original subject. On its own this new state is also harmless: for a partial match (rc < 0) the only public consumers that dereference match_data->subject all go through pcre2_substring_length_bynumber(), whose still-present offset check turns the inconsistency into a clean PCRE2_ERROR_INVALIDOFFSET return, and pcre2_substring_list_get() refuses a partial match_data outright; the new pcre2_get_subject() returns the copy together with its (self-consistent) shortened length. Only the composition is unsafe: the invariant whose guard the first commit deleted is exactly the invariant the second commit's new code breaks, so pcre2_substring_copy_bynumber() now memcpy()s from copy + ovector[stringnumber*2] with absolute offsets into an allocation that only covers the tail from start_offset - a heap out-of-bounds read (READ of 20 bytes, 259 bytes past a 21-byte region under ASan). A correct fix has to reason across both commits: repairing 4fb2f0c1's diff alone (e.g. reverting to a full-subject copy) still leaves the substring layer one dropped guard away from the same overflow for any other producer of offset/subject inconsistency, while repairing 7830094c's diff alone (re-adding the check) leaves the second commit's match_data permanently self-inconsistent - the published ovector and the copied subject disagree about their origin, an inconsistency every present and future consumer of match_data->subject is exposed to. The sound repair makes the two commits agree (copy the whole subject, or publish offsets relative to start_offset) and keeps offset validation at the point where the subject is actually read.
